The scenario must specify how she obtains the safety assessment at the meeting (e.g., printed copy) or acknowledge that she will not have it, which affects her vote.

second_review.reasoning: The scenario correctly models the evidence: Lindqvist receives updated safety data on March 10, prepares a review (half-day), and circulates it via email. Osei and Patel receive it before the meeting; Doyle does not due to retreat. At the meeting, Osei presents the review verbally, so Doyle hears it. Osei then puts the motion. Patel votes approve (favorable review), Doyle votes approve (follows safety assessment), Osei votes approve (current data now favorable). 3-0 majority approves. The terminal is produced by the vote action affordance, not by initialization. All causally necessary participants and processes are included. Uncertainties are preserved (review content not specified, but it presents data; members interpret it favorably).
